about: Fusion CX is a Kolkata-based customer experience (CX) and BPO provider delivering voice, email, chat and social support, plus AI data services, from 40 delivery centres across 13 countries. It serves 208 customers (22 Fortune 1000) in telecom and utilities, healthcare, BFSI, retail and travel, and has grown partly through acquisitions. It had 13,735 CX employees as of June 30, 2026.

objects.purpose: Repayment/prepayment of certain borrowings of the Company and subsidiaries
Investment in step-down subsidiaries (Omind Technologies Inc and Omind Technologies Pvt Ltd) for upgrading IT tools Arya and MindVoice
Unidentified acquisitions, strategic initiatives and general corporate purposes

names: P N S Business Private Limited
promoters.background: Pankaj Dhanuka and Kishore Saraogi co-founded the company in 2004 with 22 and 27 years of BPO/CX experience. P N S Business and Rasish Consultants are the Promoter Selling Shareholders (Rs 101 crore OFS each).

concentration.note: Top 10 customers were 52.17% of FY26 revenue (49.84% in Q1 FY27). 88.71% of FY26 revenue came from outside India, mostly North America.

litigation_note: Against the Company: 5 criminal, 12 tax and 4 material civil proceedings, aggregate about Rs 83.93 crore. Against subsidiaries: 2 criminal, 9 tax, 8 civil, about Rs 96.73 crore. Contingent liabilities (tax disputes) Rs 9.90 crore as of June 30, 2026.
strengths: Global delivery network of 40 centres in 13 countries with 24x7 support in 28 languages.
Revenue grew 36.8% in FY26 and PAT more than doubled to Rs 169.84 crore.
Track record of buying and integrating CX companies, which added capabilities and customers.
In-house AI tools (via Omind) are moving the business towards a more productised, tech-led CX model.
Spread across telecom/utilities (47%), healthcare, BFSI, retail and travel verticals; 22 Fortune 1000 customers.
Operating cash flow of Rs 264.22 crore in FY26; debt-to-equity improved to 0.48 from 0.86.
Reported RoNW of 30.74% and EBITDA margin of 18.14% in FY26, both rising for three years.

risks.title: High customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 customers gave 52.17% of FY26 revenue (41.04% in FY24, 49.84% in Q1 FY27). Loss of a key client would hurt revenue.

risks.title: Heavy overseas dependence and currency risk
risks.detail: 88.71% of FY26 revenue is from outside India, mainly North America; there is no hedging, so USD moves hit margins.

risks.title: Significant outstanding litigation
risks.detail: Proceedings against the Company total about Rs 83.93 crore (5 criminal, 12 tax, 4 civil) and against subsidiaries about Rs 96.73 crore.

risks.title: Debt and covenants
risks.detail: Borrowings were Rs 322.05 crore as of Aug 31, 2026; loans carry restrictive covenants and are secured by assets and promoter/group guarantees.

risks.title: Goodwill and intangibles are largest assets
risks.detail: Goodwill plus other intangibles were about Rs 371 crore at Mar-26 (about 27% of total assets); impairment would hit profits.

risks.title: Short contracts and low switching costs
risks.detail: Most contracts run under 24 months and many can be terminated at short notice without penalty.

risks.title: Acquisition-led growth and related-party dealings
risks.detail: Growth relies on acquisitions that may not integrate well; the company gave loans to and has regular dealings (rent, electricity, services) with promoter-group firms such as Windows Technologies.

risks.title: High attrition and employee cost
risks.detail: Voluntary attrition was 26.50% in FY26 (31.20% in Q1 FY27); employee cost is 65.62% of revenue.
